payload.headline: Microsoft edges up to 492.85 above support; hold and dip-buy swing plan unchanged

summary.thesis: Microsoft's sales and profit margins keep improving, but free cash flow is shrinking and the stock already prices in fast cash growth, so it is fairly valued against its own history and not cheap.
summary.decision: Long-term: hold, and add only at 474.82. Swing: keep yesterday's plan, buying a dip to 485.06 with a stop at 475.34 and a target of 503.99.
summary.act_at: Add at 474.82; swing buy at 485.06, stop 475.34, target 503.99

payload.happening: The stock closed at 492.85, up 0.6%. That is just above its strongest support zone, 485.58–490.27, which has held 7 times, and below the falling 20-day average at 514.56. There is no new news since the last note, and the next earnings report is on 2027-01-27.
payload.business: Three things describe the business itself: demand, margins and cash. Demand is strong. Sales grew 18.8% from a year earlier in the latest quarter, up from 18.3% two quarters ago, and trailing revenue reached 346.4B against 293.8B a year before. Margins are improving. The operating margin (profit from operations per dollar of sales) rose to 47.1% from 46.27%. Cash is the weak spot. Free cash flow (cash left after running the business and paying for investment) fell to 60.0B from 78.0B, so only 17.31% of sales turns into free cash. The filings say each dollar invested now earns 30¢ a year, against 51¢ three years ago. In other words, heavy spending is not paying back yet. The balance sheet is not at risk: net cash (cash minus debt) is 29.0B and available liquidity is 64.5B. Analyst estimates are also moving up. Next-year EPS (earnings per share) is 24.2, against 23.68 30 days ago. What is at risk is the payback on that spending, not demand or solvency. The 4 new risk headings in the annual report and the 'tech market in a downtrend' macro view affect sentiment more than the business.

worth.text: The methods disagree sharply. A discounted cash flow model values the company by the cash it can produce in the future. Starting from today's 60.0B of free cash flow, it gives 183.71 (bear), 222.45 (base) and 295.41 (bull), all far below the price. To justify today's price, free cash flow would have to start growing at 39.4% a year. Even 30% starting growth only gives 350.66. A second method uses the stock's own sales-multiple history: what investors have paid per dollar of sales over the past 5 years. That gives 474.82, 534.4 and 591.77, so the price sits inside a fair band. Today's price-to-sales of 10.6 is at the 32nd percentile of its own 5-year history but well above the peer median of 3.7. On earnings, the stock trades at 25.7 times trailing EPS and 20.4 times next year's estimate. The gap between methods comes down to one question: does the shrunken cash flow recover? The cash-flow model assumes today's 60.0B is the real base. The history method assumes the spending eventually turns back into cash.
worth.key_assumption: The spending that cut free cash flow from 78.0B to 60.0B turns back into cash, so the stock's own sales-multiple history is a fair guide and today's cash flow is not.

bull: Sales growth sped up to 18.8% from 18.3% two quarters ago, so demand is not fading.
The operating margin rose to 47.1% from 46.27%, so the company keeps more profit from each dollar of sales.
Analysts raised next-year EPS to 24.2 from 23.68 over 30 days, which puts the stock at 20.4 times next year's earnings.
bear: Free cash flow fell to 60.0B from 78.0B, and each invested dollar now earns 30¢ against 51¢ three years ago.
The price needs free cash flow to start growing at 39.4% a year. The cash-flow model's base value is only 222.45.
Price-to-sales is 10.6, against a peer median of 3.7, which leaves little room for a miss.

levels.what: Today's close sits inside the 474.82–534.4 fair range. Nothing here calls for selling, and it is not cheap enough to add.
The bottom of the fair range, just below the 475.34–485.06 support zone. This is the add level.
The middle of the own-history range and the top of the fair band used here. Above it the stock is no longer fair on any measure, so trim there.

longterm.why: The business is getting stronger, but free cash flow is shrinking and two of the three valuation measures lean expensive. Hold, add only at 474.82, and trim above 534.4.

swing.why: The price held above the 485.58–490.27 support zone, so the plan stands. Buy on a dip to 485.06 rather than chasing 492.85, with a stop at 475.34. The target is 503.99, the bottom of the first resistance zone, because the 20-day average is falling and the stock is moving sideways in a range.

decision.timing: Options expiring 2026-12-18 price a 7.4% move, so the swing target fits in that window. Close any swing position before the 2027-01-27 report, which options expiring 2027-02-19 price at a 14.3% move. Long-term money beyond the 474.82 add waits for that report's free-cash-flow figure.

change_mind: A close below 474.82, under both the fair range and the 475.34–485.06 support zone: no new adds and no swing entries until the 2027-01-27 report.
The 2027-01-27 report shows trailing free cash flow below 60.0B: the history-based range would lose its support, and the view would move from hold toward trim.
A close above 523.42, the top of the upper resistance zone, with next-year EPS estimates still above 23.68: the range would be broken upward, and the swing target would move up to that zone.
payload.what_changed: Unchanged: the hold and the swing plan stand, confirmed by the close of 492.85 holding above the 485.58–490.27 support zone with no new news.
payload.label: Research, not advice.
